name: Tomato
description: The tomato is a juicy, red fruit commonly used as a vegetable in cooking. Rich in lycopene and vitamin C, it is a staple of Italian, Mexican, and Mediterranean cuisines.

name: Garlic
description: Garlic is a pungent, flavorful bulb used worldwide as a base flavoring. Contains allicin, which has antimicrobial properties. Essential in French, Italian, Asian, and Mediterranean cooking.

name: Onion
description: Onions form the flavor backbone of countless dishes worldwide. They can be raw and sharp, or caramelized to sweet and complex. Yellow, white, and red varieties each have distinct uses.

name: Chicken Breast
description: Lean, versatile white meat from chicken. High in protein and low in fat, making it a staple of healthy cooking. Mild flavor pairs well with a wide range of spices and sauces.

name: Pasta
description: Dried or fresh pasta is made from durum wheat semolina. A cornerstone of Italian cuisine with hundreds of shapes. Provides slow-release carbohydrates and pairs with sauces from simple aglio e olio to complex ragù.

name: Olive Oil
description: Pressed from olives, this heart-healthy oil is fundamental to Mediterranean cooking. Extra virgin olive oil has a fruity, peppery flavor. High in monounsaturated fats and polyphenols.

name: Egg
description: Eggs are among the most versatile foods, used in baking, frying, poaching, scrambling. Rich in complete protein, choline, and fat-soluble vitamins. The yolk contains most of the fat and flavor.

name: Butter
description: Butter is made from churned cream and is prized for its rich, creamy flavor. Used in everything from sauces to pastries. Brown butter (beurre noisette) develops deep nutty notes.

name: Lemon
description: Lemons provide bright acidity that balances richness in dishes. The zest contains aromatic oils, while the juice adds tartness. Used in everything from vinaigrettes to desserts to cocktails.

name: Basil
description: Fresh basil has a sweet, clove-like aroma with peppery notes. Essential in Italian cooking, particularly pesto. Pairs beautifully with tomato. Thai basil has an anise-like flavor different from Italian.

name: Black Pepper
description: The world's most traded spice. Black pepper adds heat and pungency through piperine. Freshly ground pepper is significantly more aromatic than pre-ground. Used in virtually every cuisine.

name: Salt
description: Sodium chloride is fundamental to all cooking. It enhances flavor, preserves food, and affects texture. Kosher salt, sea salt, and table salt differ in grain size and trace minerals.

name: Flour
description: All-purpose flour is the foundation of baking. Protein content determines gluten development: bread flour (high protein) for chewy breads, cake flour (low protein) for tender cakes. Whole wheat retains the bran and germ.

name: Carrot
description: Carrots are sweet root vegetables rich in beta-carotene. Eaten raw, roasted, or used to build flavor in soups and stocks. The sweetness intensifies with cooking. Baby carrots are just regular carrots trimmed down.

name: Potato
description: Potatoes are starchy tubers that form the base of cuisines worldwide. Russets are best for baking and frying, Yukons for mashing and roasting, and waxy varieties for salads. Technically nightshades.

name: Spinach
description: Spinach is a nutrient-dense leafy green packed with iron, folate, and vitamins K and A. Mild when raw, it wilts dramatically when cooked. Used in salads, sautés, pasta fillings, and smoothies.

name: Cheddar Cheese
description: Cheddar is a sharp, cow's milk cheese that ranges from mild to extra sharp. An English original (Somerset), now produced worldwide. Melts well, pairs with apples, beer, and charcuterie.

name: Broccoli
description: Broccoli is a cruciferous vegetable high in vitamin C, K, and cancer-fighting compounds. Can be eaten raw or roasted to develop nutty, caramelized flavors. Related to cauliflower, cabbage, and kale.

name: Salmon
description: Atlantic or Pacific salmon is prized for its rich flavor and high omega-3 content. Can be eaten raw (sushi, gravlax), cured, smoked, or cooked. The fat gives it a silky texture and forgiving cooking window.

name: Rice
description: Rice feeds over half the world's population. Long-grain (basmati, jasmine) stays fluffy; short-grain (arborio, sushi rice) is sticky. Brown rice retains the bran for more fiber and nutrients.

name: Cumin
description: Cumin has a warm, earthy, slightly bitter flavor essential in Indian, Mexican, and Middle Eastern cuisines. Whole seeds can be toasted; ground cumin is more convenient. Pairs with coriander, chili, and turmeric.

name: Parmesan Cheese
description: Parmigiano-Reggiano is an aged Italian hard cheese with a complex, nutty, salty, crystalline texture. True Parmesan must be made in Emilia-Romagna. Central to pasta, risotto, and soups. The rind adds flavor to stocks.

name: Ginger
description: Fresh ginger has a bright, spicy, slightly floral heat different from ground ginger. Essential in Asian cuisines — stir-fries, soups, marinades. Also used in baking and cocktails. Has anti-inflammatory properties.

name: Mushroom
description: Mushrooms add deep umami flavor through glutamates. Button/cremini/portobello are the same species at different maturities. Shiitake, oyster, and porcini have distinct flavors. Dried mushrooms are intensely flavored.

name: Bell Pepper
description: Bell peppers range from crisp and grassy (green) to sweet and fruity (red, yellow, orange). Green peppers are unripe; red are fully ripe and highest in vitamins. Excellent raw, roasted, or stuffed.

name: Coriander
description: Coriander seeds have a warm, citrusy, slightly floral flavor. The leaves (cilantro) taste bright, citrusy, and soapy to some people (genetic trait). Both used widely in Mexican, Indian, and Thai cooking.

name: Coconut Milk
description: Coconut milk is the liquid extracted from grated coconut flesh. Rich and creamy, it forms the base of Thai curries, Indian kormas, and Caribbean stews. Full-fat is richer; light has less coconut fat.

name: Lime
description: Lime provides sharper, more floral acidity than lemon. Essential in Mexican, Thai, Vietnamese, and Caribbean cooking. Key lime is smaller and more intensely flavored. Zest adds aromatic citrus oils.

name: Chili Pepper
description: Chili peppers range from mild (Anaheim, poblano) to fiery (habanero, ghost pepper). Heat comes from capsaicin. Dried, smoked, or fresh chilies each have distinct flavors beyond just heat.

name: Avocado
description: Avocados are creamy, rich fruits high in monounsaturated fat. They ripen off the tree and go from firm to perfectly ripe to overripe quickly. Essential for guacamole; pairs with eggs, citrus, and spice.

name: Honey
description: Honey is the only food that never spoils. Flavor varies enormously by floral source: clover is mild, buckwheat is bold, manuka is medicinal. Used in dressings, marinades, baking, and teas.

name: Soy Sauce
description: Soy sauce is a fermented condiment made from soybeans, wheat, salt, and water. Light soy sauce is saltier and thinner; dark is thicker and sweeter. A fundamental umami source in Asian cooking.

name: Thyme
description: Thyme has a woody, earthy, slightly floral aroma. It holds up well in long cooking, making it ideal for braises, stocks, and roasts. Pairs with poultry, lamb, and root vegetables.

name: Rosemary
description: Rosemary has a strong, piney, resinous aroma. It stands up to high heat — excellent for roasting meats and potatoes. Use sparingly as it can overpower. Pairs with lamb, chicken, and olive oil.

name: Parsley
description: Flat-leaf (Italian) parsley has a brighter flavor than curly. Often used as a finishing herb to add freshness. Cornerstone of French fines herbes and gremolata. Packed with vitamin K and C.

name: Chickpea
description: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans) are high-protein legumes central to Middle Eastern, Indian, and Mediterranean cooking. Used whole in salads and stews, or pureed into hummus. Aquafaba (chickpea water) is an egg white substitute.

name: Beef
description: Beef flavor comes from fat marbling and aging. Different cuts have different uses: tender cuts (ribeye, tenderloin) for quick cooking; tougher cuts (chuck, brisket) for slow braises. Grades: Prime > Choice > Select.

name: Milk
description: Cow's milk provides calcium, protein, and fat. Whole milk (3.5% fat) has the richest flavor; skim is almost fat-free. Used in baking, sauces, and drinks. Lactose-free and plant-based milks are alternatives.

name: Apple
description: Apples range from tart (Granny Smith) to sweet (Fuji, Gala) to complex (Honeycrisp). Eaten raw, cooked, juiced, or fermented into cider. Pectin in the skin is excellent for jams and pies.

name: Banana
description: Bananas are sweet, creamy tropical fruits. Underripe bananas are starchy and firm; overripe are sweeter and perfect for baking. Rich in potassium and B6. Plantains are less sweet cooking bananas.

name: Beef Stock
description: Rich beef stock is made by simmering bones and vegetables for hours. Forms the base of French onion soup, braises, and pan sauces. Gelatin from bones gives it body. Store-bought is a pale substitute.

name: Paprika
description: Paprika is ground dried red peppers ranging from sweet and mild to hot and smoky. Hungarian and Spanish (pimentón) are the best known. Smoked paprika adds depth without heat. Essential in paella, goulash, and deviled eggs.

name: Celery
description: Celery provides a fresh, slightly bitter, herbal flavor. Part of the French mirepoix trio (with onion and carrot). The leaves are more flavorful than the stalks. Very low in calories but provides fiber.

name: Chocolate
description: Chocolate is made from fermented, dried, and processed cacao beans. Dark chocolate (70%+ cacao) is intensely flavored and less sweet. Milk chocolate is creamier. Cocoa powder is unsweetened ground cacao.

name: Vanilla
description: Vanilla is the second most expensive spice after saffron (by weight). The pods of an orchid, vanilla has a floral, creamy, sweet-complex flavor. Extract is more convenient; paste has seeds. Essential in baking.

name: Kale
description: Kale is one of the most nutrient-dense foods. Massaging raw kale breaks down its toughness for salads. Lacinto/Tuscan kale is more tender than curly kale. Chips, smoothies, and sautés are popular preparations.

name: Eggplant
description: Eggplant (aubergine) absorbs flavors beautifully. Roasted eggplant becomes silky and smoky. Salting draws out bitterness and moisture. Essential in baba ghanoush, ratatouille, and moussaka.

name: Zucchini
description: Zucchini (courgette) has a mild, slightly sweet flavor. Best when small and firm; large zucchini become watery. Excellent grilled, sautéed, spiralized as noodles, or in bread. Related to other summer squash.

name: Oregano
description: Oregano has a strong, peppery, slightly bitter flavor. More pungent dried than fresh. Greek and Italian oregano differ in intensity. Essential in pizza sauce, Greek salads, and Mexican cooking.

name: Lamb
description: Lamb has a distinctive, sweet, gamey flavor that mellows with age. Young lamb (spring lamb) is most tender. Excellent roasted (leg, shoulder), grilled (chops), or slow-braised. Pairs with mint, rosemary, and garlic.

name: Shrimp
description: Shrimp are quick-cooking, versatile seafood. They turn pink and curl when cooked — cook just until done or they become rubbery. Wild-caught has better flavor than farmed. Used in stir-fries, pasta, tacos, and cocktails.
